name: Mountain Pose
benefits: Encourages upright posture and body awareness.
Builds a stable foundation for standing poses.
Helps improve balance and concentration.
steps: Stand tall with feet together or hip-width apart.
Distribute your weight evenly across both feet.
Lengthen your spine, relax your shoulders and let your arms rest by your sides.
Breathe steadily and keep your gaze soft.
cautions: If standing balance is difficult, practise near a wall or chair.

name: Tree Pose
benefits: Challenges balance and concentration.
Strengthens the standing leg and ankle muscles.
Encourages an upright posture.
steps: Begin in Mountain Pose.
Shift your weight onto one foot.
Place the other foot against your ankle or inner calf; avoid pressing on the knee.
Bring your hands together at your chest or raise them overhead.
Hold while breathing steadily, then change sides.
cautions: Use a wall for support. Avoid placing the foot directly on the knee.

name: Warrior I
benefits: Builds strength in the legs.
Opens the chest and front of the hips.
Develops stability and body awareness.
steps: Stand with feet wide apart and turn one foot forward.
Bend the front knee while keeping it aligned over the ankle.
Angle the back foot slightly outward and ground its outer edge.
Raise your arms if comfortable and keep your torso upright.
Breathe, then repeat on the other side.
cautions: Shorten your stance if the hips or knees feel strained. Do not force the backbend.

name: Warrior II
benefits: Strengthens legs and shoulders.
Builds balance and stamina.
Encourages hip mobility.
steps: Stand with feet wide apart and turn your front toes outward.
Bend the front knee, keeping it tracking in the same direction as the toes.
Extend both arms at shoulder height.
Gaze over the front hand and keep your torso upright.
Repeat on the other side.
cautions: Keep the front knee comfortable and avoid letting it collapse inward.

name: Triangle Pose
benefits: Stretches the sides of the torso and legs.
Challenges balance and coordination.
Encourages spinal length.
steps: Stand with feet wide and turn one foot outward.
Extend your arms and reach your torso over the front leg.
Rest your lower hand on your shin or a yoga block.
Extend the top arm upward if comfortable.
Keep both sides of the torso long and repeat.
cautions: Use a block and avoid forcing your hand to the floor. Keep your neck comfortable.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
benefits: Stretches the back of the legs and shoulders.
Builds strength through the arms and upper body.
Can be used as a transition or resting shape.
steps: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders.
Spread your fingers and tuck your toes.
Lift your hips up and back, forming an inverted V shape.
Bend your knees as needed and lengthen your spine.
Press evenly through both hands and breathe.
cautions: Modify or skip if wrist, shoulder or eye-pressure concerns make the pose unsuitable.

name: Child's Pose
benefits: Offers a gentle resting position.
Allows the back and hips to relax.
Encourages slow, steady breathing.
steps: Kneel on the mat and bring your big toes together.
Separate your knees to a comfortable width.
Fold your torso forward and rest your forehead on the mat or a cushion.
Extend your arms forward or place them beside your body.
Breathe comfortably.
cautions: Use a cushion under the hips or forehead. Avoid if kneeling is painful.

name: Cobra Pose
benefits: Gently strengthens back muscles.
Opens the front of the chest.
Encourages spinal extension and body awareness.
steps: Lie on your stomach with legs extended.
Place palms beside your lower ribs and keep elbows close.
Press the tops of your feet into the mat.
Use your back muscles to lift your chest; use your hands lightly.
Keep shoulders away from ears and lower slowly.
cautions: Keep the lift low and pain-free. Avoid or seek guidance with an active back injury, pregnancy or recent abdominal surgery.

name: Bridge Pose
benefits: Strengthens glutes and the back of the body.
Gently opens the front of the hips and chest.
Develops awareness of controlled movement.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart.
Place arms by your sides and keep feet parallel.
Press through your feet and lift your hips comfortably.
Keep knees pointing forward and breathe.
Lower your spine slowly.
cautions: Avoid turning your head while lifted. Stop if you feel neck or back pain.
video: Setu Bandha bridge pose yoga tutorial

name: Cat–Cow
benefits: Moves the spine through gentle flexion and extension.
Coordinates movement with breathing.
Can help prepare the body for practice.
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Inhale, gently tilt the pelvis and broaden the chest.
Exhale, round the spine and gently draw the belly in.
Move slowly between the two shapes with your breath.
cautions: Keep the movement small and comfortable; avoid forcing the neck.

name: Butterfly Pose
benefits: Gently stretches the inner thighs.
Encourages an upright seated posture.
Can be used in a calming floor sequence.
steps: Sit with the soles of your feet together.
Let your knees fall outward without pushing them down.
Hold your feet or ankles and sit tall.
Stay upright or hinge forward slightly from the hips.
Breathe steadily.
cautions: Sit on a folded blanket if your hips or knees feel uncomfortable. Do not bounce the knees.
video: Baddha Konasana butterfly pose yoga tutorial

name: Seated Forward Bend
benefits: Stretches the back of the legs.
Encourages a gentle forward hinge at the hips.
Can support a quiet, mindful practice.
steps: Sit with legs extended and spine tall.
Flex your feet gently and soften your knees if needed.
Inhale to lengthen your spine.
Exhale and hinge forward from the hips, holding your legs or feet.
Keep the neck relaxed and breathe.
cautions: Avoid pulling yourself down. Modify for back pain or hamstring injury.
video: Paschimottanasana seated forward bend yoga tutorial

name: Corpse Pose
benefits: Provides time for rest after practice.
Encourages awareness of natural breathing.
Supports a calm transition out of movement.
steps: Lie comfortably on your back.
Let your legs rest apart and arms relax by your sides.
Close your eyes if comfortable.
Allow your breath to return to its natural rhythm.
To finish, gently move fingers and toes and roll to one side.
cautions: Place a bolster under your knees or lie on your side if lying flat is uncomfortable.

name: Happy Baby
benefits: Gently moves the hips through a comfortable range.
Can release tension after a movement sequence.
Encourages relaxed breathing.
steps: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your chest.
Hold the backs of your thighs, ankles or outer feet.
Let your knees move toward your armpits without forcing.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed.
Breathe slowly.
cautions: Hold behind the thighs if gripping the feet strains your shoulders or hips.
video: Ananda Balasana happy baby yoga tutorial

name: Low Lunge
benefits: Stretches the front of the hip on the back leg.
Builds balance and lower-body awareness.
Can prepare the body for standing sequences.
steps: Begin in a low lunge with one foot forward and the back knee lowered.
Place hands on your front thigh or raise arms if comfortable.
Keep the front knee over the ankle.
Gently shift the hips forward without compressing the lower back.
Switch sides.
cautions: Pad the back knee and keep the range gentle.

name: Pigeon Pose
benefits: Provides a hip stretch when appropriately supported.
Encourages mindful control of hip position.
Can be included in a floor-based mobility practice.
steps: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind the wrist.
Angle the shin only as far as comfortable.
Extend the other leg behind you.
Support the front hip with a folded blanket if needed.
Stay upright or fold forward gently; switch sides.
cautions: Do not force the front shin parallel to the mat. Choose a supine figure-four stretch if the knee feels pressured.
video: pigeon pose yoga beginner modification tutorial

name: Plank Pose
benefits: Builds whole-body strength and stability.
Challenges core and shoulder endurance.
Develops alignment awareness.
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Step one foot back and then the other.
Align shoulders over wrists and lengthen through your heels.
Keep your body in one long line and breathe.
Lower your knees to modify.
cautions: Stop if wrists or shoulders hurt. Use forearms or knees for a modification.

name: Chair Pose
benefits: Strengthens thighs and glutes.
Challenges balance and postural control.
Builds lower-body endurance.
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and send hips back as if sitting into a chair.
Keep weight grounded through the feet.
Raise arms only as far as comfortable.
Keep breathing and rise slowly.
cautions: Keep knees comfortable and avoid sinking lower than your mobility allows.

name: Boat Pose
benefits: Challenges abdominal and hip-flexor strength.
Develops balance while seated.
Encourages controlled posture.
steps: Sit with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Lean back slightly while keeping your spine long.
Lift one foot at a time; keep knees bent.
Extend arms forward or hold behind thighs.
Lower feet if your back rounds or effort becomes uncomfortable.
cautions: Keep knees bent or feet down. Avoid if it causes back discomfort.

name: Legs Up the Wall
benefits: Offers a supported resting position.
Encourages a quiet breathing practice.
Can feel soothing after a long day.
steps: Sit sideways next to a wall.
Lie back and gently swing your legs up the wall.
Move your hips a comfortable distance from the wall.
Rest your arms by your sides and breathe naturally.
Bend your knees and roll to one side to exit.
cautions: Avoid or seek medical advice first with glaucoma, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or conditions where inversion is unsuitable.
video: legs up the wall restorative yoga tutorial

name: Eagle Pose
benefits: Challenges single-leg balance.
Works coordination and concentration.
Creates a shoulder and upper-back stretch variation.
steps: Stand tall and soften one knee.
Cross the other thigh over it, using toes as a kickstand if needed.
Cross arms at the elbows and bring palms together or hold shoulders.
Sit slightly into the standing leg and breathe.
Unwind and change sides.
cautions: Use a wall for balance and skip the leg wrap if knees feel uncomfortable.

name: Dancer Pose
benefits: Challenges balance and coordination.
Combines a standing balance with a front-body stretch.
Builds body awareness and control.
steps: Stand tall and shift weight to one foot.
Bend the other knee and hold the ankle or foot behind you.
Reach the opposite arm forward or upward.
Press the foot gently into the hand while keeping the chest lifted.
Use a wall or strap and change sides.
cautions: Practise with support. Avoid forcing the backbend or gripping the foot if the shoulder is uncomfortable.

name: Camel Pose
benefits: Opens the front of the body.
Challenges back-body strength and control.
Encourages mindful spinal extension.
steps: Kneel with knees hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Lengthen through the spine and lift the chest.
Keep hips stacked over knees as you gently lean back.
Keep hands on hips or reach for heels only if comfortable.
Return upright slowly.
cautions: Use blocks beside your ankles. Avoid if this backbend causes neck or lower-back pain.

name: Bow Pose
benefits: Challenges back and glute strength.
Stretches the front of the body.
Develops coordinated movement and control.
steps: Lie on your stomach and bend your knees.
Reach back to hold your ankles or use a strap.
Inhale and gently lift your chest and thighs only as comfortable.
Keep the movement smooth and breathe.
Release slowly.
cautions: Skip if you have back, neck or shoulder injury, or if pressure on the abdomen is unsuitable.

name: Easy Seated Pose
benefits: Provides a comfortable position for breathing or meditation.
Encourages an upright seated posture.
Supports stillness and concentration.
steps: Sit on a folded blanket or cushion.
Cross your shins comfortably without forcing the knees.
Rest hands on thighs and lengthen your spine.
Relax your shoulders and breathe naturally.
cautions: Sit on a chair if cross-legged sitting causes knee or hip discomfort.

name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold
benefits: Stretches the inner thighs and back of the legs.
Encourages a hip hinge and spinal length.
Can be used as a calming standing stretch.
steps: Stand with feet wide and parallel.
Place hands on hips and lengthen your spine.
Hinge forward from your hips.
Rest hands on blocks or the floor without forcing.
Bend knees slightly and rise slowly.
cautions: Keep knees soft and avoid if forward folding aggravates back symptoms.

name: Sphinx Pose
benefits: Offers a gentle supported spinal extension.
Opens the front of the chest.
Can be an accessible alternative to a higher cobra.
steps: Lie on your stomach with legs relaxed.
Place elbows under or slightly ahead of shoulders.
Rest forearms on the mat and gently lift your chest.
Keep the back of your neck long.
Breathe and lower slowly.
cautions: Move elbows forward or lower your chest if the lower back feels compressed.

name: Staff Pose
benefits: Builds awareness of upright seated alignment.
Engages the legs and postural muscles.
Provides a starting position for seated poses.
steps: Sit with both legs extended in front.
Place hands beside your hips, using blocks if needed.
Flex feet gently and lengthen your spine.
Relax shoulders and look forward.
Breathe steadily.
cautions: Sit on a folded blanket and bend knees slightly if your back rounds.

name: Extended Side Angle
benefits: Strengthens the legs.
Stretches the side body.
Develops balance and coordination.
steps: Take a wide stance and turn the front foot outward.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
Rest forearm lightly on thigh or hand on a block.
Reach the top arm overhead to lengthen the side body.
Repeat on the other side.
cautions: Use a block and keep the front knee aligned with the toes.
video: Utthita Parsvakonasana extended side angle yoga

name: Thread the Needle
benefits: Provides a gentle shoulder and upper-back rotation.
Encourages comfortable spinal movement.
Can ease into a restorative floor sequence.
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Slide one arm underneath the other, palm facing up.
Lower that shoulder and the side of your head toward the mat.
Keep hips above knees and breathe gently.
Return slowly and switch sides.
cautions: Keep the range small if shoulder or neck discomfort occurs.
